content.text:
Operator
Thank you for standing by, and Welcome to Dime Community Bancshares, Inc. Q2 Earnings Conference Call. Before we begin, the company would like to remind you that discussions during this call contain forward-looking statements made under the safe harbor provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Such statements are subject to risks, uncertainties, and factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in any such statements, including as set forth in today's press release and the company's filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, to which we refer you. During this call, references will be made to non-GAAP financial measures as supplemental measures to review and assess operating performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with US GAAP.
For information about non-GAAP measures and for reconciliation to GAAP, please refer to today's earnings release. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speaker's presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, you will need to press star one one on your telephone. You will then hear an automated message advising your hand is raised. To withdraw your question, please press star one again. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Stuart Lubow, President and CEO. Please go ahead.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Good morning. Thank you, Lisa, and thank you all for joining us this morning for our quarterly earnings call. With me today is Avi Reddy, our CFO. In Q2, Dime continued to execute on our growth plan. The momentum in our business is strong and we grew core deposits by over $300 million and business loans by over $200 million. The strong growth in core deposits has enabled us to reduce our wholesale funding position substantially since year-end. As a result, the net interest margin increased by 20 basis points in the quarter. We were pleased with the increase in the margin and believe Q1 2024 was a trough for this cycle in terms of both net interest income and NIM.
Our cost of deposits declined on a linked quarter basis, and since the end of Q2, deposits have continued to remain stable to down. Going forward, we expect a slow and steady build in NIM absent any rate cuts. Rate cuts and the eventual repricing of our legacy lower coupon fixed and adjustable rate loan portfolios should accelerate NIM expansion as we get into the latter half of 2025 and 2026, and this will drive a structurally higher NIM. Over the past month, we have successfully raised $75 million in subordinated debt. At the end of Q2, our total capital ratio was 14.5%, and we now rank at the absolute top end of our local peer group in terms of total capital. Capital is obviously important in executing our growth strategy.
Asset quality continues to remain solid with NPAs down 29% on a linked quarter basis. We plan to file our 10-Q next week and expect to report that classified assets will also be down approximately 14% on a linked quarter basis. We recently received regulatory approval for a new branch location in Westchester County. In fact, I was in White Plains just last week for a business reception we hosted with many important new and prospective clients and proud of our ability to expand Dime franchising into this new attractive market. Subsequent to our Q1 earnings call, where we announced the onboarding of six deposit gathering teams, we've onboarded another two deposit gathering teams in May and June. One of these teams is based in Williamsburg, a market that is very familiar to Dime and where we were founded.
The second team is based in Manhattan. Additionally, we hired an exceptional banker to build out our not-for-profit lending vertical. I am proud of the company-wide effort in terms of recruiting and integrating all these bankers into the Dime umbrella. Clearly, our recruiting efforts over the past year have been successful. Our deposit gathering groups are up over $1 billion of total deposits, and our middle market C&I group helped drive strong business loan growth this quarter. In the quarters ahead, we expect the healthcare vertical to begin to meaningfully contribute to the loan growth and the diversification of our balance sheet as they have built a substantial loan pipeline at an attractive yields. In summary, I am very optimistic about the trajectory that Dime is on.
Our market continues to be significantly disrupted, and the strategic offense we've been playing is paying off in the numbers. With that, I will turn it over to Avi.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Thank you, Stuart. Reported EPS was $0.43 per share, an increase of 5% over the linked quarter. In line with the mid-quarter update we provided in June, we saw meaningful NIM expansion to the tune of 20 basis points. NIM expansion was driven by the strong year-to-date growth in core deposits and our business loan portfolio, as well as the proactive reduction in higher cost wholesale funding. Non-interest income for Q2 was $11.8 million. This included a gain on the sale of a branch that we executed a sale leaseback on. Core cash operating expenses for Q2, excluding intangible amortization, was $55.4 million. We have recruited approximately 65 revenue generating bankers over the course of the past five quarters, including 15 deposit gathering teams, a fully built out healthcare vertical, and most recently, a not-for-profit vertical.
We expect the revenue generation from these hires to far outweigh the start-up expenses associated with the organic build-out of all these groups in the years ahead. We had a $5.6 million loan loss provision this quarter. The allowance to loans increased to 72 basis points. Our CET1 ratio is above 10%, and our total capital ratio of 14.5% is now best in class amongst our local peer group. Next, I'll provide some thoughts on the NIM expenses and balance sheet growth. With respect to the NIM, we called out in the earnings release that there was a 4 basis point benefit from the payoff of a loan that was previously on non-accrual status.
In addition, the sub-debt offering, which closed on the last day of the quarter, is expected to have a three basis points downward impact on the NIM going forward. As such, the base NIM to work from for modeling purposes for future quarters is closer to 2.34. As Stuart said, we expect a slow and steady improvement in the NIM until the impact of rate cuts kick in. We also have a significant repricing opportunity in our adjustable and fixed rate loan portfolios that's expected to kick in in the second half of 2025 and 2026.
To give you a sense of the repricing opportunity, in the second half of 2025 and in 2026, we have approximately $2 billion of adjustable and fixed rate loans across the loan portfolio at a weighted average rate of 3.9% that either reprice or mature in that time frame. Assuming a conservative 225 basis point spread for those loans over the forward five-year Treasury, we should see a substantial 35 basis point increase in the NIM as these loans reset to higher rates in 2025 and 2026. With respect to expenses, we expect core cash operating expenses for Q3 to be approximately $57 million, and we expect to hold that quarterly run rate with very nominal growth in 2025.
We are working on a few company-wide initiatives that should drop to the bottom line in 2025, and this should result in very nominal expense growth for 2025. With respect to our positioning on lending, we anticipate continued growth in our business lending portfolio. Growth in the business portfolio will offset declines in multifamily and CRE, while we are still servicing existing relationships. On an aggregate basis, we expect the loan portfolio to be up low single-digits for the second half of the year. With that, I'll turn the call back to Lisa, and we'll be happy to take all your questions.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Thank you. As a reminder, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one one on your telephone. We also ask that you wait to hear your name and company announced before you proceed with your question. One moment for the first question. Our first question today is coming from Mark Fitzgibbon of Piper Sandler. Your line is open.
Greg Zingone
Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Hey, good morning, guys. This is Greg Zingone stepping in for Mark at the moment. How are you?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Hey, Greg. How you doing?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Great. How are you?
Greg Zingone
Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Just curious, what was your spot NIM for June?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. What I tried to point out in the prepared remarks, Greg, was we had around four basis points from the payoff of our previous non-accrual loan. All that happened in the month of June, so the June NIM was a little inflated. If you back that out, you know, the spot NIM would have probably been around 2.36%, 2.37% for the month of June. We also mentioned that, you know, the sub debt offering closed at the end of June, so that'll have an impact going forward. Probably around 2.36% to 2.37% ex the sub debt for June.
Greg Zingone
Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Okay. On the $5.5 million provision, is that a good run rate for us to think about for the remainder of the year?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Well, we evaluate the provision every quarter based on economic conditions, so it's really gonna be a function of, you know, what the Moody's forecasts are on a going forward basis. I think right now we feel, you know, pretty adequately provisioned. We built the reserve a basis point here. So it's really gonna be a function of, you know, how the Moody's estimates come out, Greg.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. As we continue to book new loans, C&I and business-related loans, obviously, those provisions are somewhat higher. You know, there'll be just in terms of the ongoing shift in the loan portfolio, there'll be you know, some provisioning associated with that that will change relative to the model.
Greg Zingone
Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Okay. Lastly, how big of a push do you plan to make in Westchester? Is adding more teams or more branches in Westchester a priority going forward?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
I think, you know, we've got two teams up there now. We've just gotten approval for a full service or limited service branch up there. We're not really looking to open up retail locations. It's really more second story, you know, business related growth. You know, for now, I could see us bringing on more teams over time. I don't see us opening up a lot more bricks and mortar up there in terms of branch locations.
Greg Zingone
Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Awesome. Thank you guys.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Thanks, Greg.
Operator
Thank you. One moment for the next question. Our next question will be coming from Manuel Navas of D.A. Davidson. Your line is open.
Manuel Navas
SVP and Senior Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
Hey, good morning, fellas. I appreciate. I think I just missed the OpEx guide for next quarter. Could you just reiterate that? Then any color you can add on some of the things you're looking at for next year. You're saying you're gonna have nominal expense growth. Could you highlight or discuss any of those initiatives in greater detail, or is it too early to say?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah, we're just going through our budgeting process now, Manuel. I think as we get towards the end of the year into really our January call, we'll be able to outline all of those in detail. The guidance was, you know, we probably expect to be around $57 million, you know, in Q3, you know, kind of hold that for the rest of the year. But our goal is, you know, for next year to have very, very nominal growth, you know, absent any, you know, additional team hiring, you know, opportunity that could take place next year. That's pretty much the guidance. At this point, I think we'll have more details as we get, you know, get into our December and January timeframe once we get through the budgeting season.
Manuel Navas
SVP and Senior Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
I really appreciate that. That leads me to my next question. What's kind of the pipeline on hires? Has it kind of calmed down? Are you still seeing talent out there that's interesting? What's just kind of an update on hiring, the hiring process?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. You know, we're still talking to folks. There's still talent out there, both on both sides of the balance sheet, both on the deposit side and on the lending side. We've obviously been busy on both sides of the balance sheet. We brought on, you know, a group of C&I lenders, and they've, you know, really have begun contributing in a significant way. Our healthcare group pipeline is very significant. I think there's gonna soon be some meaningful loan volume this quarter in that business as well. We are exploring other teams in terms of C&I business. Yeah, there's some opportunity.
I think as we get later in the year, you know, as folks get closer to year-end and bonuses and whatnot, that's gonna slow down a little bit, but we are planting the seeds into next year. You know, I do think there's some opportunity. I think we proved that, you know, we're the bank to be in terms of opportunity and bringing their customers over. You know, we've opened, you know, 3,000 to 4,000, like, new business accounts and relationship accounts with the new teams that are just starting to fund. You know, we're almost at $1.1 billion in new deposits, nearly half of that DDA. You know, the model and the thesis that we have has proved out. I think, you know, we're looked at as a place to go in terms of opportunity. I really do think there's a lot to come in the future.
Manuel Navas
SVP and Senior Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
Is healthcare gonna be a big chunk of the low single digit growth in the second half of this year? I think you've given pipeline in the past for that group. Is that something that's disclosable today?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Sure. I mean, our pipeline in the healthcare business is $172 million at an average rate of 7.80%. And you know, but our C&I pipeline is $430 million at an average rate of 8.5%. You know, it's across the board and it's really, you know, again, following what we've been saying for the last year in terms of diversification. You know, we're quite encouraged by the build out of both our middle market C&I business, our healthcare business. Even our residential group is up substantially in terms of pipeline. They have over $60 million in the pipeline at a 6.5% rate, all adjustable rate mortgages, you know, again, you know, we're out there and we're doing business. We're very encouraged.
Manuel Navas
SVP and Senior Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
If I just shift to the NIM for a moment. I really appreciate the repricing opportunity, second half of next year into 2026. More near term, if we do get a rate cut in September, could the slow and steady NIM increases accelerate a bit in Q4?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yes. Yes.
Manuel Navas
SVP and Senior Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
Okay.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. I mean, I think [crosstalk] I think we're seeing, you know, just month-over-month with the new originations and repricing of what loans we do have that are repricing, this year. We're seeing a slow and steady growth, you know, in terms of loan yields, and deposit yields are flat to down. Just the natural progression is positive. Certainly with a rate cut in September and possibly one later in the year, you know, we could see that accelerate, you know, quite a bit. You know, just month-to-date, for example, our yields on a loan are up over three basis points. You know, we expect that to accelerate with this quarter's new originations and repricing.
You know, again, we're optimistic. You know, as I said, absent rate cuts, we're going to see a you know, a slow and steady grind up. Certainly the rate cuts are gonna help, you know, accelerate that growth.
Manuel Navas
SVP and Senior Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
My last question is that repricing opportunity doesn't include any. It just includes the forward curve for the second half of 2025 into 2026. It's just the loan side. It doesn't include expectations on rate cuts in there, correct? Is that the right way to think about that analysis?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Correct. Yep, just off the forward curve, Manuel. The comment was, you know, we have, you know, $2 billion in the back half of 2025 and 2026 at a rate of 3.90%. Just follow the forward curve and that's, you know, you know, which is around 4% for the five-year going forward. You should see a 35 basis point, you know, increase in the NIM overall, just solely because of that. Now on top of that, we are remixing the loan portfolio. That's obviously adding, as we said, around four to five basis points every quarter to the NIM. Then you layer on top of that the deposit growth that we have.
We still have around $750 million of brokered on the balance sheet. We've obviously paid down a lot of our short-term FHLB borrowings. That was the first step in the balance sheet evolution. The brokered is still at $750. You know, as the new teams bring in deposits, as our lending teams bring in deposits, that's going to help offset the brokered deposits on the balance sheet. I think the message here is we don't need rate cuts to see an upward bias in the NIM. With rate cuts, we're going to have an even greater increase in the NIM.
Once the repricing opportunity kicks in, you know, the NIM is really going to accelerate at that point in time back and probably higher than where we were in the last cycle based on what our models are showing.
Manuel Navas
SVP and Senior Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
That's great. I really appreciate the commentary. Thank you very much.
Operator
Thank you. Our next question will be coming from Steve Moss of Raymond James. Your line is open.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
Good morning.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Hey, Steve.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Hey, Steve.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
Just following up on deposits here. Stuart, I think you said balances on deposits were stable to down at the beginning of the call. Just kind of curious here, you know, a healthy step up in the deposit growth with all the teams you've added here. Is it possible that we could see that pace continue this quarter?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
The second part to that. [crosstalk] Go ahead.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
What I said was yields on deposits were stable to down. We're seeing steady growth on the deposit side. We expect continued growth on the deposit side.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
Okay. Perhaps at a similar pace to what we saw this past quarter?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah, I don't think we don't think about it on a quarterly basis, Steve. Obviously, you know, in Q1 and Q2, there was, you know, significant disruption with one of our competitors. Sometimes it ebbs and flows. I mean, the way we look at it is the groups that have come on, right? The average tenure of the groups on a weighted average basis is only seven to eight months at the bank. They have a substantial runway in front of them to do that. You know, we're measuring it in terms of years as opposed to quarters. I think, you know, a year from now we're going to be substantially higher than where we are right now. Every individual quarter you have seasonality, deposits coming in, deposits coming out.
The other way we track this too, Steve, is accounts. We're continuing to see accounts open, you know, every day, every week. You know, very bullish about them bringing over more and more deposits over time.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
Okay. Could you share with us how many accounts were open this quarter?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
This quarter we probably had, I would say, close to around 700 to 800 accounts that were open.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
In terms of, just curious what the blended cost of funds you're seeing on the deposits coming over these days?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. Probably say around between $250 and $270± from the new groups, because as Stuart said, substantial portion of it is in DDA, probably 40% to 45% DDA of the stuff that's coming in. So it's between $250 and $275.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
Okay. Appreciate that. In terms of the drivers here on the lower classified down 14% quarter-over-quarter. Just curious to get some incremental color around those drivers.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah, we should have all the detail in the 10-Q. We just provide an expectation right now. I think multifamily is down around $15 to 20 million. I think C&I and owner-occupied are down, you know, the rest basically. Investor CRE is basically flat. All the detail will be in our 10-Q next week, Steve.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
Appreciate that. Okay. I guess just, you know, last one for me here in terms of, you know, it sounds like you guys remain active on the hiring front or at least interested, you know. Do you expect like a steady pace of ads in the second half for additional teams, or is it more maybe 2025?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah, I think it's more 2025. As we're getting toward the end of the year, folks tend to have, you know, the view of, well, I'm gonna stay where I am for now. I got bonuses coming up. It's probably more towards, you know, the end of Q1 2025. Although there probably might be some opportunity on the lending side with some teams that, I think, you know may be available, and, you know, we are talking to seriously. I think on a deposit side, it's probably more, you know, geared toward early 2025.
Steve Moss
Managing Director, Raymond James
Okay, great. Really appreciate all the color. Nice quarter.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one one on your telephone. Our next question will be coming from Christopher O'Connell of KBW. Your line is open.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Hey, good morning.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Hey, Chris. Good morning.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Hey, Chris.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Yeah, just wanted to start off on the NIM and, you know, apologize if I miss anything. From what I understand, you know, slow and steady progress until there's rate cuts from here in the back half of the year . And that's inclusive of the sub debt offering, correct? And kind of minus the non-accrual recovery. Are you guys thinking the NIM will progress and be up from the 2.37 June NIM range, ex the non-accrual recovery?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah, no. Chris, in my prepared remarks, what I said was the base NIM to use is 2.34. The 2.34 excludes the four basis points from the non-accrual interest recovery and then the three basis points from the sub-debt. I'd start with the 2.34 and use the slow and steady and upward bias off of that base. As we've said, the loan yields are going up probably, you know, four to five basis points every quarter on an average basis. That's going to help. Obviously, if you see stabilization in the cost of deposits, you know, you're gonna see a natural upward progression in the NIM. I think that's the case till there's rate cuts.
Once there's rate cuts, we obviously have more, you know, deposits than assets that we can reprice. That's gonna help, you know, help us, I'd say, starting in Q4 into Q1 and Q2 of next year. Then, you know, layer on top of that the substantial repricing opportunity that really starts, you know, in the second half of 2025. It's gonna be a layered, you know, approach in terms of the NIM. Then I think you also have to factor into all of that the new deposit teams that are coming, that are bringing in deposits. As I said, you know, a rate of between 2.50 and 2.75 versus the brokered cost right now, which is 5.35.
I think if you put all of that together, you know, we're pretty confident that, you know, as we get into, you know, back half of 2025 and 2026, then the NIM structurally will be a lot higher than where it is right now.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Great. That's helpful. Then as you guys are, you know, it sounds like very good quarter multifamily on the, you know, criticized, classifieds, no NPLs. Can you just remind us of, you know, how much you guys have maturing in the rent regulated portfolio in the second half of the year? Just anything that you've been seeing from your customers in terms of, just, you know, any qualitative data, as to, you know, what you've been seeing in terms of either debt service coverage ratios or just conversations with the customers, you know, for what's matured year-to-date.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. I'll start off with what's coming due and then Stuart will add some qualitative comments. I mean, in Q3, we probably have around $10 million on the rent regulated side, and in Q4 we have, I think, $15-20 million. It's very modest this year in terms of what's remaining. In Q2, for example, we probably had around $45 million of rent regulated loans that were supposed to reprice. Around $20 million of that satisfied, around $25 million of that repriced. And we've had no issues associated with them. Probably like a 1/3, 2/3 split as of the last quarter in terms of satisfactions and repricings. Stuart can probably give you some color qualitatively on that.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. I mean, we haven't had a lot of conversations with customers, you know, the phones are not ringing off the hook in terms of issues or problems. Obviously, our NPLs and delinquencies are stable to down. You know, it's, you know, we're monitoring everything. We haven't seen a significant change in debt service coverages. Actually, you know, overall probably, you know, a lot of it has actually gone to the positive in terms of growth in debt service coverage. I'd say 75% to 80% of the portfolio, year over year, has had debt service coverage improvement, you know, at this point, you know, we continue to monitor and you know and certainly stay in contact with customers where necessary, but we're not seeing any significant issues at this point.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Great. Then just on the expense discussions of, you know, jumps up to $57 million next quarter. I'm assuming a lot of that's in compensation from the new hires. Then it sounds like you think, you know, that level can hold, you know, relatively flat, you know, into 2025. Just, you know, what are some of the puts and takes, you know, I'm assuming there's merit increase, et cetera, in 2025. Where you guys think that you have opportunities to kind of save and kind of limit the overall expense growth, you know, from here into 2025.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. I think all of that's fair, Chris. I think, you know, for the second half of this year, around $57 million± is probably a good range. Obviously the merit increases go into effect, really on 1 April 2022. You know, Q1 next year is gonna be pretty consistent with where the second half of this year is gonna be. I mean, look, we've always managed expenses efficiently. Like you said, you know, we're gonna see an uptick in salary and comp expense, especially as the new groups, you know, are performing very well. You know, there's accruals and such to think about on a going-forward basis.
We're working, like I said, when I answered Manuel's question, we're working on a few, you know, company-wide initiatives. We'll probably have more to disclose, when we get into early next year. I think the guidance for next year is very nominal growth. I wouldn't say flat because, you know, we're obviously investing in our businesses, you know, throughout the year. We're gonna be very judicious, as we always are. As you know, see the NIM, you know, trajectory, you know, improve over time, I think that's gonna give us a little bit of room to invest in the business, as well. Look, we're very happy with the early performance of the groups. The groups are basically, you know, better than break even, at this point in time.
There's no additional, you know, fixed costs that are coming in, you know, beyond what, you know, the $57 million run rate that we have right now. Look, we'll have more to say, you know, then. I think just down the road, you know, there will come a time when we're able to grow the balance sheet a little bit more. At that point in time, you know, I think we'd, you know, our expense to asset ratio will also naturally start coming down. You know, we've historically managed the company, you know, between 150 and 155. We're probably closer to 160 to 165 right now. You know, we do see that coming down in the years ahead, as if and when balance sheet growth picks up.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Great. Then any small, but any color on the drop in customer service fees this quarter. Was last quarter kind of an unusually strong quarter, or should we take it as like a blend of the two?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. We just had some rollover fees last quarter on some loans basically that we're repricing. So as I said earlier, we had more multifamily loans this quarter that actually satisfied versus repriced. That's where that fits in. Last quarter we had more loans. In Q1, more loans that took the rollover option, and that's where that goes in there. I would say, look, there's a couple of seasonal items here and there, you know, that come in and out, but you know, nothing material.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Got it. I know you guys are usually cautious on this, but you know, any sense of just, you know, outside of the amount of fixed maturities and everything happening in the second half of 2025 into 2026, but you know, what the impact of each 25 basis point cut would be on the margin?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah, I think it's gonna be, you know, obviously the first rate cut and the second rate cut, you know, it's gonna, part of it's gonna depend on the competition, you know, in terms of what they're doing. That said, I will say our deposit base is more skewed towards commercial customers, and we have more money markets than time deposits in our base. So which should lend itself to more, you know, in terms of having more benefit from rate cuts than a lot of our peers, right?
You know, if you look at the balance sheet right now, around 31% to 32% is variable rate in terms of the loan portfolio. Obviously 30% of the balance sheet is DDA, you know, on the deposit side of the balance sheet. We probably have, you know, some deposits that are, you know, cost less than 1%, and so it's gonna be harder to change the rates on those. I would say, you know, by and large, you know, our goal is really to get the margin back, you know, to that 3%+ area, which is gonna drive higher, you know, returns overall for the company. Our internal models show us getting there, you know, latter part of 2025, you know, into 2026.
How it happens between here and there could be choppy up and down in an individual quarter, but there's definitely gonna be, you know, a level of benefit from rate cuts.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah. We do have, you know, as Avi said before, we do have $700 million of brokered that we'll be able to move down very quickly in terms of a rate cut. Plus, we have about $1.8 billion of municipals that are also, you know, easily moved in terms of a rate cut. You know, look, we're prepared. We've already segregated the portfolio in terms of when a rate cut happens, you know, which buckets are gonna move and how much. I mean, we're pretty optimistic, but, you know, we're a little cautious at this point because obviously, you know, competition's gonna play a bit of a role there as well.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Got it. Last one for me. Just, what's a good tax rate going forward?
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Yeah, I think around 27%, Chris. We had a couple of discrete items this quarter, so I'd use 27% going forward.
Christopher O'Connell
Director of Equity Research, KBW
Great. Thank you.
Avinash Reddy
EVP and CFO, Dime Community Bancshares
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. There are no more questions in the queue. This does conclude today's Q&A session. I would now like to turn the call back over to Stuart Lubow for closing remarks. Please go ahead.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime Community Bancshares
Thank you, Lisa. Thank you all for joining us today. I'd like to thank our dedicated employees and our shareholders for their continued support, and I look forward to speaking with you after Q3.
Operator
Thank you for joining today's conference call. You may all disconnect.

events.title: Q2 2024 Dime Community Bancshares Inc Earnings Call

content.text:
Operator
Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Dime Community Bancshares Q1 Earnings Call. At this time, all participants are in listen-only mode. After the speaker's presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the session, you will need to press star one, one on your telephone. You will then hear an automated message advising your hand is raised. To withdraw your question, please press star one, one again. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker today, Stuart Lubow, President and CEO. Please go ahead.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Thank you, Marvin, and thank you all for joining us this morning for our Q1 earnings call. With me today is Avi Reddy, our CFO. Dime has begun 2024 on solid footing and on a positive growth trajectory. In the Q1, we grew core deposits by 19% on an annual basis, paid down our Federal Home Loan Bank borrowings by 41%, maintained solid asset quality, increased our risk-based capital ratios, prudently managed expenses, and importantly, saw our net interest margin expand in the month of March versus year-end and January levels. We have been active on the hiring front, and since the middle of March, we've added over 30 extremely talented revenue-producing bankers. I would like to provide some color on why these bankers joined Dime.
As you know, the first group of bankers we hired in 2023 have been very strong advocates of Dime and have gotten the word out that Dime is the premier platform for talented bankers. They have seen firsthand how nimble we are as a bank, how our staff is aligned to make the customer experience outstanding, and how flat our organizational structure is. The bankers hired in 2023 have grown their deposit portfolios to approximately $600 million. Suffice to say, we have proved that our business model provides conducive environment for talented bankers to succeed. Secondly, our technology and treasury management systems are state-of-the-art and superior to all other local banks. We know this because all the groups that we recruited in 2024 did detailed demos of our systems, and to a person, they were all significantly impressed.
Our feedback from new customers has been outstanding. Finally, Dime's brand name and reputation in our local market is second to none. We have 60 branches from Montauk to Manhattan, and our reputation has always been that of a strong community bank. Customers like working with strong community banks where they have access to decision-makers and get things done quickly. Four of the deposit groups that we hired are based in Brooklyn. One is based in the Five Towns area of Nassau County. We're also very excited to enter Westchester County, specifically White Plains. Westchester is a market we've looked at for a long time, and we finally found the right banker to lead our efforts there. In Q1, we closed the first healthcare loan in our new vertical.
Our healthcare team is actively in the market at the moment, and our healthcare pipeline is robust at $150 million with a weighted average yield of 8.8%. We expect this vertical to contribute to our overall loan growth and aid in the diversification of our balance sheet. As I mentioned on our prior earnings call, this is an important component of our strategic plan. In summary, I am pleased that the investments that we've put into the business in 2023 are starting to pay off, and I'm very optimistic about the hires we have just announced. Dime has been navigating the macro environment well and will, while simultaneously playing strategic offense, and taking advantage of the opportunities in our market. With that, I will turn it over to Avi.
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Thank you, Stu. Reported EPS was $0.41 per share. In line with our expectations, the NIM bottomed in January and expanded to 2.23% in the month of March. The exit NIM would have been even higher by around 3 basis points had we not carried some excess liquidity in February and March as a precaution, given the disruption caused by a large regional bank in our footprint. We normalized our liquidity position towards the middle to the end of March, and as such, the Q2 should not have this liquidity-related drag going forward. We are cognizant of the overall environment and continue to manage expenses prudently. Our focus is on being as efficient as possible. Core cash operating expenses for the Q1, excluding intangible amortization and extinguishment of debt, was $51.7 million or down 3% versus the prior quarter.
Non-interest income for Q1 was $10.5 million. This included a gain on the sale of a branch that we did a sale leaseback on. We had a $5 million loan loss provision this quarter. The allowance to loans increased to 71 basis points. In light of the overall environment, our posture as it relates to the balance sheet is to build capital methodically. This will in turn support our clients when they need it. Our Common Equity Tier 1 ratio improved to 10%, which is an optically important benchmark in our mind. Our reported total capital ratio was 13.8%. Incorporating the full impact of AOCI, it would have been 13%. As you know, the focus these days is on capital with the AOCI impact.
In this regard, compared to banks between $10 billion and 100 billion of assets, our total capital ratio inclusive of AOCI of 13% would put us in the top third of our peers. Next, I'll provide some updated thoughts on our expense guide for 2024. For those who follow Dime closely, in 2023, we were able to absorb the cost of the new deposit-gathering groups into our organization, along with the addition of various corporate staff to support them by rationalizing expenses across the organization. As part of our 2023 efforts, we significantly expanded our treasury management and back-office staff and intentionally built the bank for future expansion. As a result, we don't expect any meaningful additional staffing in corporate support areas to support the new hires we have made in 2024.
Said differently, any expense build in 2024 is primarily for revenue-generating staff that is expected to pay for itself relatively quickly. At the start of the year, we had guided to a range of $210 to 212 million of core non-interest expense ex intangible amortization. We are now increasing the guide to a range of $214 to 216 million. This represents the cost of all the new groups hired to date, and is net of the benefits of additional bank-wide efficiency initiatives we have planned for 2024. On a standalone growth basis, we expect the new group hires to begin generating pre-tax income by Q3 and be cumulatively break even inclusive of all the start-up costs in Q4.
Starting in 2025, they will contribute to growth in earnings and book value per share versus our prior standalone numbers without the 2024 new hires. With respect to our positioning on lending, our strategy is to ensure we continue to support our key clients, and we continue to see growth in our business lending portfolio. Growth in the business portfolio will offset declines in multifamily and CRE, where we are still servicing existing relationships. On an aggregate basis, we expect loans year over year to be up in the low single digits. With that, I'll turn the call back to Marvin, and we'll be happy to take your questions.
Operator
Thank you. At this time, we will conduct the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, you will need to press star one, one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. To withdraw your question, please press star one, one again. Please stand by while we compile the Q&A roster. Our first question comes from the line of Steve Moss of Raymond James. Your line is now open.
Steve Moss
Analyst, Raymond James
Hi, good morning.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Hi, Steve.
Steve Moss
Analyst, Raymond James
It's Stu. You know, maybe just starting with the new hires here from Signature. Just, you know, curious if you could size up the deposit potential and any specialties with the group.
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah, sure. Steve, I'll take that to start with. I mean, the groups, you know, as we said in our press release when we put it out, you know, most recently, they managed $several billion of deposits. You know, the groups really fit with our existing business model, very plain vanilla community commercial banking. Four of the groups are based in Brooklyn, where we have an existing branch presence. One of them is based in the Five Towns area, and then the last one is in Westchester. The groups in general are slightly bigger than the groups we hired last year. So, the teams are generally, you know, between four and six people, which is higher than what we had last year.
I think we've laid out the groups last year at around $600 million of deposits. You know, our expectations for these groups are to be higher than that, you know, given their book of business, as well as, you know, given the size of these groups. As well as, you know, some of the improvements that we made over the course of the year in terms of, you know, our technology, our platforms, our operations. They're really, you know, gonna start hitting the ground running here in the Q1 onwards.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Yeah. Just in terms of some context. Last year, the groups we hired were managing about $1 billion in deposits. If you recall, I said at that time, if we got to 50%, I thought it would be a home run in terms of what they brought over. You know, they're currently at $600 million. You know, we're excited about the new hires. I will say in the first three weeks of their coming on board, we've opened up over 1,000 accounts for the groups, you know, in total. You know, very active. We have people working weekends opening accounts. You know, we're excited by the opportunity and, you know, we're very positive that this is gonna accrue greatly to our benefit.
Steve Moss
Analyst, Raymond James
Okay, appreciate that. Just as we think about the deposits coming on here, you know, I hear you guys in the press release highlighting that it starts to be core funded here. Should we expect a similar type of cost of funds for the deposits coming on like last year's groups?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. I mean, they pretty much had a very similar book in terms of, you know, very high percentage of DDA. Obviously, the rate environment is, you know, even more competitive at this point, you know, given the Fed's posture. Our focus is really on, you know, core deposits, low-cost deposits. As you said, Steve, you know, the plan over the next 6 to 12 months is to use that to continue to pay down FHLB and broker deposits, and really drive NIM expansion through that going forward.
Steve Moss
Analyst, Raymond James
Okay. Just in terms of the loan pipeline here. You know, hear you on the healthcare vertical, but just in aggregate, just curious, you know, what's the size of the total pipeline and kind of, you know, how are you thinking about that?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
All right. You know, today it's $1.1 billion with average yields of 8.14%. In C&I and owner-occupied CRE it's over $600 million. As I mentioned, the healthcare is approaching—is actually today a little higher, almost $180 million. The important thing is, you know, the other thing I want to mention is we have approximately $200 million, $206 million approved waiting to close that we expect to close in the next 30 to 90 days. We think the next several months are going to be very busy in terms of new loan bookings.
The pipeline is active. We are seeing, you know, some nice new activity coming in. As we announced earlier this month, we did hire two middle market bankers from another institution, who already have some deals in the pipeline as well, and they're primarily C&I lenders. You know, we are seeing demand pick up and activity pick up, and our pipeline is pretty robust.
Steve Moss
Analyst, Raymond James
Okay. Appreciate that. Maybe just one last one here. Just curious on the NPA. Looks like maybe just one NPA in ADC. Just curious as to the dynamics with that property, and any color you can give there.
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yes, yes Steve, we actually did a reappraisal on that and, you know, very, very well secured from a collateral perspective. There's a couple of tenants that are gonna be moving in to that. So we don't expect any loss content at all. But just from an accounting standpoint, we conservatively moved it into NPA. You know, we hope to get it resolved in Q2 or Q3, but don't see any loss content there at all.
Steve Moss
Analyst, Raymond James
Okay. Maybe just to clarify, is it just kinda like a timing issue with completion and rents, or you know?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Yeah. The building is complete, 100% complete. It's tenanted with a significant medical facility. They're gonna be doing their build-out. The rent starts, you know, you know, this month, and, you know, we've got an updated evaluation, and we're pretty comfortable that, you know, this is gonna be resolved in Q2.
Steve Moss
Analyst, Raymond James
Okay. Appreciate all the color. I'll step back. Thanks.
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Thanks, Steve.
Operator
Thank you. One moment for our next question. Our next question comes from the line of Mark Fitzgibbon of Piper Sandler. Your line is now open.
Gregory Zingone
Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Hey, guys. This is Gregory Zingone stepping in for Mark at the moment. How are you?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Hey, Greg. How are you?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Hey, Greg.
Gregory Zingone
Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
The new expense guide as you said includes the new teams hired to date, but how many more hirings can we expect this year?
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
You know, we're still talking to several teams. We probably expect, you know, an announcement of at least one more team relatively soon. We'll continue to, you know, have conversations, and, you know, take advantage of opportunities. You know, the disruption in the marketplace has never been so great, here in the New York metropolitan area. It takes time. We've interviewed a number of teams within that are available, and, you know, I don't expect, at this point, you know, to double what we have per se, but, you know, there are still conversations happening and opportunities we believe will benefit us.
Gregory Zingone
Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Depending on how many teams you bring on board the remainder of the year, could that $214 to 216 million in expenses kinda trickle up a little higher?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. Greg, I think the way to look at it is, you know, these groups are producing revenue, right? That was my initial comment that on a cumulative basis, you know, we expect the groups to be breakeven in 2024. When you're thinking about your model going forward, it's really accretive starting in 2025 with no, you know, deterioration in 2024 from an EPS perspective. As I said also, we're not really adding any, you know, we don't really need to add any additional support staff, you know, with them because we, you know, built the company out for growth. Look, we're always judicious on expenses. We're telling you where we are right now based on, you know, who's joined the company right now.
In the future, you know, we always look to hire productive people. You know, we'll keep you updated as we go along.
Gregory Zingone
Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Okay. With all the people you're bringing on board and your expectation for accelerated balance sheet growth, do you envision needing additional capital in the near future?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. Look, I mean, the plan right now is really to remix the balance sheet, you know, with what we have. You know, we have around $700 million of FHLB on the balance sheet. Our broker deposits, while, you know, a lot lower than, you know, a lot of our local peers, is probably around ±$750 million. We really have a pathway there to remix the balance sheet by paying off some of these items. Obviously, you know, supporting our clients is the most important. We said, you know, multiple times, you know, on the investor CRE and multifamily side, we expect those to pay down slowly over time, so you're gonna get some cash flows out of that, and we're gonna grow the business portfolio.
I think with the groups that we have right now, you know, we're confident that, you know, we can remix the balance sheet. Our capital is very strong. Our Common Equity Tier 1 ratio is 10%. Like I said, our total capital ratio is 13.8%. You know, even with the impact of AOCI, it's 13%. We feel pretty good about the remixing story and supporting our clients with our existing capital base.
Gregory Zingone
Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
All right. Thank you guys so much.
Operator
Thank you. One moment for our next question. Our next question comes from the line of Manuel Navas of D.A. Davidson & Co. Your line is now open.
Manuel Navas
Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
Hey, good morning. Could you guys speak a little bit on your comfort around the reserve level, around 71 basis points? Should we kind of expect a methodical build from here?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Manuel, we're comfortable. Otherwise, we wouldn't be reporting earnings where we are. We're comfortable.
Manuel Navas
Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
Okay. How have repricings gone year to date across either multifamily or any other CRE loan?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. We've had no issues. You know, loans have repriced. I will say our criticized and classified is actually down 9% on a year-to-date basis. You know, we're probably down around $5 to 10 million on the CRE and multifamily side, and probably down around $30 to 35 million on the owner-occupied side. You know, I'd say, you know, overall it's business as usual. You know, as we've always said in the past, we don't have a lot of, you know, maturities and repricings in 2024 and 2025. You know, we're not really seeing anything unusual at this point.
Manuel Navas
Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
Great. As you think about the balance sheet remixing kind of shifting over to the NIM, it seems to be inflecting on a monthly basis. Can that kind of improved pace continue near term, in general?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. I think the way to think about the NIM, a little bit is, you know, the month of February and March was probably the first months in the last 15 to 16 months that the deposit costs actually declined. The spot deposit cost at the end of March was 2.68. The cost of deposits for the full quarter was 2.70. You know, we did see some competition in December and January and the January NIM was really a bottom in our mind. On a going forward basis, especially with these new groups coming on, you know, you should see, you know, stability in the cost of deposits. Then it's just gonna be a function of how, you know, quickly, you know, originations come on board.
If you go back to the month of September, the weighted average rate on the loan portfolio was around 5.20. In December, that went up to 5.29. That was based on around $200 million of originations for Q4. Q1 was a little bit slower in terms of originations, and that's just seasonal where you close a lot of loans at the end of the year. Because we did half the originations, the weighted average rate on the loans only increased by 5 basis points. You go back to Stu's point about the pipeline. If you're gonna assume around $200 million of originations every quarter, that should lead to an increase in the weighted average rate, you know, by around 8 to 10 basis points on the loan side.
On an average basis, you're probably gonna get a 4 to 5 basis point benefit on the margin there. I think overall, we, you know, we're thinking about the NIM with an upward bias going forward. Obviously the cost of deposits is the biggest piece of that. We do believe that that's stabilized to a large extent.
Manuel Navas
Research Analyst, D.A. Davidson
That's great. I really appreciate the color. Thank you, guys.
Operator
Thank you. One moment for our next question. Again, as a reminder to ask a question, you will need to press star one, one on your telephone. Our next question comes from the line of Christopher O'Connell of KBW. Your line is now open.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Hey, good morning.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Chris.
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Hey, Chris.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Just on the, you know, the deposit, new deposit team adds and kind of that break-even point that you're targeting to hit in Q4. What's the deposit level for them to hit breakeven?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. You know, on an average basis, Chris, you know, they probably should get to around, you know, call it around $400 million of deposits ±. Maybe between $350 and 400 million by that point, you know, for Q4 basically. You know, when you look at that run rate, then it starts becoming, you know, breakeven to, you know, positive at that point.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Got it. As far as the balance sheet movements in the quarter, you know, on the end of period basis, you know, the borrowings were a lot lower than on the average basis. I mean, were those paid off pretty late in the quarter? Do you have any sense of how that's gonna impact, you know, the margin going into Q2? I mean, was it included, you know, in the March 2023 margin, or is there further benefit of that coming into Q2?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. A little bit further benefit, Chris. If you look at, I mean, the easiest way to look at it is if you look at our, you know, the short-term investments that we had, it was around $300 million more this quarter than we had last quarter. For the full quarter, the impact was more. In my prepared remarks, what I tried to say was, you know, in the month of March, you know, we paid down the borrowings starting on 1 March 2024, but we were probably done by around 20 March 2024. There's probably around a 3 basis points drag even for the month of March.
That 2.23 margin for March was probably more like, you know, 2.25 to 2.26, as an exit run rate going forward, you know, into Q2. That doesn't include the benefits of any further paydowns that we'll have of borrowings or broker deposits going forward once, you know, the deposit starts coming in.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Great. You know, and I know you guys, you don't give short term, you know, margin guidance, but based on that commentary, is it kinda safe to assume that, you know, you trend back up to, you know, close to the levels that you were at into Q4 of 2023 and kind of migrate consistently upward from there as asset repricing or as kind of overall balance sheet repricing occurs going forward?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. I think you know overall the way we describe it is an upward bias. I think last quarter our guidance was you know the margin will be within a few basis points. I think without this liquidity build it would have been within a few basis points and obviously is a little bit down. You know I think it's fair to say upward bias you know the individual factors are you know stabilization in the deposit costs which helps not having a liquidity drag which helps. Then Stu's point more originations on the loan side which also help. You know as you see you know more paydowns and you know in Q3 we have some treasuries maturing. We probably have around $75 million I believe in Q3.
You know, right now the yield on those Treasuries are like 1%, so that's gonna help as well. You're gonna see a little bit of that, you know, into Q3 and into Q4. I think I'll leave it at, you know, upward bias and it'll be a function of, you know, closings on the loan side.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Great. There were some changes announced impacting, you know, the overall, you know, New York multifamily, you know, space, with the budgeting being passed in the past week or so. Any thoughts or color as to how you guys think that will impact the market and if it will be significant at all? Just any general, I guess, thoughts on, you know, the state of, you know, the New York multifamily market and how, you know, you expect to manage, you know, your exposure going forward.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Yeah. I mean, it's still a little early to, you know, to ascertain what the ultimate impact's gonna be. They still have to work out the details and, you know, it's certainly better than, you know, what the advocates wanted. It's not necessarily where all the landlords want it to be. I mean, I still think that has to work through. I think on the margin, it could've been worse and, you know, it's probably, you know, a net positive, overall. It's still gotta work through the process and we have to see how it actually, you know, affects the market.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Got it. In any sense as to, you know, were there any rent-regulated multifamily maturities in Q1? If there was, you know, where the new debt service coverage ratios were that repriced?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
Yeah. I don't have that off the top of my head, Chris, here. But we had a, you know, very small amount in Q1, probably, I don't know, ±$30 million of multifamilies and, you know, most of them took the option basically to reprice. We can follow up, you know, after the call with.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Yeah. I mean, they're all paying, they're current. You know, it was a relatively small handful of loans that repriced during the period. They just repriced and, you know, the way it works in our world is if you take the repricing, you have to pay a fee. They paid the fee and they're repricing and, you know, they're current.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Great. The, you know, the near-term outlook, I know there's, you know, zero multifamily on NPAs and zero any loans on 90 days past due. As you guys have, like, looked through, you know, the maturity schedules, which are fairly light, you know, over the next couple of quarters, I mean, is there anything, you know, that concerns you in terms of, you know, credit quality and coverage after repricing on the rent-regulated book?
Avi Reddy
CFO, Dime
No. Not especially. You know, like I said, you know, we monitor the criticized and classified very closely. The multifamily criticized classified was, I think, down, you know, $4 or 5 million. So at this point, nothing stands out.
Christopher O'Connell
Analyst, KBW
Great. Thanks for taking my questions.
Operator
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn it back to Stuart Lubow for closing remarks.
Stuart Lubow
President and CEO, Dime
Thank you, Marvin. Once again, I'd like to thank all of our team members for their support during our significant growth initiatives. Our philosophy of a single point of contact and customer-centric approach to our customers remains first and foremost. Both new and old customers are the mainstay of our organization, and our continual success will accrue not only to the benefit of our customers, but to the franchise value as well. We look forward to speaking with you all after Q2. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you for your participation in today's conference. This does conclude the program. You may now disconnect.
